title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare and say your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may sound urgent and try to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your benefits will be canceled unless you verify your Social Security number and pay a $99 reactivation fee right now."
red_flags: Caller threatens to cancel your benefits
Asks for your Social Security number or payment
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text message saying you have a package waiting, with a link to track or reschedule delivery. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information or installs malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please confirm your details here: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to click for more info
Poor spelling or odd web addresses
what_to_do: Do not click the link; delete the message.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails that look like they are from the Social Security Administration. They claim there is a problem with your account and ask you to click a link or provide personal information.
example_message: "We noticed suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please verify your information to avoid suspension."
red_flags: Email says your Social Security number is at risk
Asks you to click a link or reply with personal info
Email address looks odd or unofficial
what_to_do: Do not reply or click links; report the email to the Social Security Administration.

title: Romance Scams on Facebook
how_it_works: Someone you meet on Facebook quickly forms a close relationship and then asks for money, often for an emergency or travel. They may use fake photos and stories to gain your trust.
example_message: "I care about you so much, but I need help paying for my plane ticket to come see you. Can you send me $500?"
red_flags: Person you never met asks for money
Stories about emergencies or travel problems
Refuses to video chat or meet in person
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven’t met in person.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: You get a call from someone pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away. They may beg you not to tell anyone else.
example_message: "Grandma, it’s me! I’m in jail and need bail money. Please don’t tell Mom and Dad—can you wire me $1,000?"
red_flags: Caller claims to be a relative in trouble
Requests for wire transfers or gift cards
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check the story.
